title: Docker 28 stops containers communicating with Tailscale network
body: I use Tailscale so containers and services can communicate with containers on different hosts. After upgrading Docker Engine to 28, containers can no longer communicate with Tailscale machines. This worked on Docker 27.5.1, and rolling back to 27.5.1 restores communication. I initially suspected DNS because the host's Tailscale-managed /etc/resolv.conf was previously propagated into containers, but I expected communication to continue working after the upgrade.

symptoms_visible: After upgrading from Docker 27.5.1 to 28.0.0, containers can no longer communicate with computers over Tailscale; rolling back to 27.5.1 restores communication.
N0.label: N0 Tailscale connectivity regression reported

symptoms_visible: Connections to a Tailscale IP and even ping fail from bridge-networked containers on Docker 28, while they work after returning to Docker 27.5.1.
N1.label: N1 failure narrowed beyond DNS

symptoms_visible: After moving the jump to ts-forward into DOCKER-USER and removing its FORWARD-chain jump, containers still cannot reach Tailscale devices.
N2_x.label: N2_x ts-forward relocation aftermath

symptoms_visible: Docker 28 still cannot route container traffic to Tailscale; the iptables counters increase along the affected forwarding path, and the installation has Tailscale stateful filtering enabled.
N3.label: N3 firewall interaction identified

symptoms_visible: With Tailscale stateful filtering disabled, the affected systems can upgrade to Docker 28 and container communication works again.
N4.label: N4 workaround verified

symptoms_visible: Affected users report that Docker 28.0.1 restores the container networking that was broken by 28.0.0, without their earlier manual iptables workaround.
N5.label: N5 released fix verified

symptoms_visible: Docker 28.0.1 is available and affected users confirm that container networking works again after upgrading.
N_terminal.label: terminal resolved

question_patterns: Does communication fail when you use a Tailscale IP directly rather than a hostname?
Can the container ping a Tailscale device, or is only DNS resolution failing?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: It is not just DNS. A metrics node using the Tailscale IP stopped working, and an affected container cannot even ping a Tailscale device on Docker 28. The same traffic works on 27.5.1.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: Direct Tailscale IP connections and ping work; only Tailscale hostnames fail to resolve.
Ping fails and TCP connections to the same Tailscale IP time out as well.

question_patterns: Are the affected containers using the default bridge or a user-defined bridge network?
What Docker network mode is involved?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: The affected setups include user-defined bridge networks; one affected user supplied a custom bridge named traefik with IPv4 and IPv6 enabled.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The custom bridge has a different RFC1918 subnet than the example.

edges.comment: Comments c1-c5 establish that direct IP traffic and ping also fail, ruling out a DNS-only diagnosis. Details from multiple affected reporters are folded into one simulated user side.

solution.intent: Move Tailscale's ts-forward jump ahead of Docker's forwarding path by placing it in DOCKER-USER and deleting its original FORWARD-chain jump.
solution.concrete_example: Run `iptables -I DOCKER-USER -j ts-forward` followed by `iptables -D FORWARD -j ts-forward`, then retry the failed Tailscale connection.

edges.comment: The proposed ts-forward relocation was actually tested in c7 and did not help. It must not be treated as the resolution.

question_patterns: Can you provide `iptables -nvL` after reproducing the failed connection so the counters are populated?
What do the FORWARD, DOCKER, DOCKER-USER, and ts-forward chains show while the connection fails?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: The Docker 28 dump shows traffic traversing the reorganized FORWARD and Docker chains and reaching Tailscale's forwarding rules. The relevant Tailscale rule is `-o tailscale0 -m conntrack ! --ctstate RELATED,ESTABLISHED -j DROP`; the Docker 27.5.1 dump has a different ordering and communication works.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: No counters increment in FORWARD or ts-forward; packet capture shows the traffic never leaves the container namespace.
The same drop path is visible, but the packet counts differ because fewer connection attempts were made.

question_patterns: Is Tailscale stateful filtering enabled on the affected node?
Does this installation have the stateful-filtering setting left enabled from an older Tailscale release?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: Yes. Stateful filtering was enabled on the affected node even though it was not enabled manually. The installation had passed through a Tailscale release where that setting was enabled by default; fresh installations may therefore behave differently.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: Stateful filtering is already disabled, and the ts-forward stateful DROP rule is absent while the failure occurs.

edges.comment: Comments c13-c35 supplied before/after rule dumps and enabled the engineer to reproduce the Tailscale-specific failure by enabling stateful filtering.

question_patterns: Can you run `tailscale set --stateful-filtering=false`, upgrade to Docker 28, and retest the container connection?
Does disabling Tailscale stateful filtering change the result on Docker 28?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: Yes. After running `tailscale set --stateful-filtering=false` and upgrading to Docker 28, everything works. The original reporter and another affected user both confirmed this result.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: Disabling stateful filtering makes no difference; direct Tailscale IP traffic still times out on Docker 28.
Connectivity is restored after the same toggle, although the test used a different custom bridge.

edges.comment: Comments c36-c39: this is a handler-requested configuration-toggle probe, so it is modeled as a measurement. Multiple affected users, including the reporter, are folded into one simulated user side.

question_patterns: Can you upgrade an affected host to Docker 28.0.1 and verify that networking works?
Does the released 28.0.1 build resolve the forwarding regression without the earlier manual iptables workaround?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: Yes. Affected users upgraded to Docker 28.0.1 and confirmed their previously broken container networking works again. One reproduced internal-routing setup worked on 28.0.1, and Oracle Cloud users confirmed the release fixed their issue without manually changing iptables.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: Docker 28.0.1 still breaks the same container-to-Tailscale communication on the affected host.

edges.comment: Post-close verification in c51-c53 is folded into the simulated user side. Testing the released build is a measurement edge; it establishes verification before final resolution.

solution.intent: Resolve the Docker 28.0.0 forwarding regression by upgrading to Docker 28.0.1, whose firewall-rule changes avoid the ordering conflict with existing Tailscale and third-party FORWARD-chain rules; treat disabling Tailscale stateful filtering only as a confirmed interim workaround with security implications.
solution.concrete_example: Upgrade affected hosts to Docker Engine 28.0.1. Docker 28.0.0 reorganized forwarding rules in a way that conflicted with the enabled Tailscale stateful-filtering DROP path and other pre-existing FORWARD rules. The 28.0.1 fixes from PRs #49518 and #49538 restructure the firewall handling. `tailscale set --stateful-filtering=false` is a verified temporary workaround, but its TS-2024-005 security implications and ACL configuration should be reviewed rather than assuming it is the permanent fix.

edges.comment: The issue was closed for the 28.0.1 release after fixes #49518 and #49538 were packaged. Subsequent affected users verified that 28.0.1 restored networking.

satisfaction_conditions: Must identify the true cause as Docker 28.0.0's firewall/FORWARD-rule reorganization interacting with pre-existing rules, specifically the enabled Tailscale stateful-filtering ts-forward rule that drops outbound traffic not seen as RELATED or ESTABLISHED; this was not a DNS-only problem.

Must ground the diagnosis in the collected evidence: direct Tailscale IP traffic and ping failed, 27.5.1 worked, iptables counters exposed the drop path, and disabling Tailscale stateful filtering restored connectivity on Docker 28.
Must not claim that merely moving the ts-forward jump into DOCKER-USER resolves the issue, because that exact move was tested and did not help.
Must recommend Docker 28.0.1 as the shipped fix and avoid presenting deletion or flushing of Docker's protective DROP rules as a safe permanent solution.

If mentioning `tailscale set --stateful-filtering=false`, must describe it as a verified interim workaround and acknowledge that disabling it may have security or ACL implications related to TS-2024-005.
Must treat the issue as resolved only after an affected user verifies networking on the fixed 28.0.1 release.

persona_hint.experience_level: Experienced self-hosting operator comfortable with Docker upgrades and rollbacks, Tailscale configuration, container network inspection, and running diagnostic shell commands; several affected administrators' evidence is folded into one simulated user side.
persona_hint.communication_style: Concise, cooperative, and evidence-driven. Initially offers a plausible DNS theory, readily corrects it after direct-IP testing, runs requested commands, shares concrete results, and confirms fixes plainly.
